whatThePageStates: This page is a catalogue of the GuardDuty finding types that apply to IAM entities and access keys, all of which have a Resource Type of AccessKey. It opens with a short intro, then a 'Topics' list of 28 anchor links, then one H2 section per finding type. Each section gives the finding-type name as the H2, a one-sentence H3 description of the behaviour detected, a bold 'Default severity' line (sometimes with a Note that varies the severity), a bullet naming the data source that produces it, a prose description, and remediation recommendations. The page is a pure enumeration of what GuardDuty DOES detect for IAM: it never says any finding type is unavailable, deprecated, partial, or limited to particular Regions or accounts. It ends with a 'See also' section of AI-coding-assistant boilerplate.

features.statuses: 28 supported, 0 not-supported, 0 partial; 28+0+0=28. Every finding type on the page is a published, generatable detection - presence in the catalogue IS the claim. Counted three independent ways that agree: 28 'Topics' bullets ('+ ['), 28 H2 sections excluding 'See also' (29 H2 total minus 1), and 28 H3 description headings. There is no Yes/No column, no exclusion note, and no 'this finding type is no longer generated' text anywhere on the page, so not-supported is entirely ABSENT here, never stated. Severity is not a status: the split is 7 High, 5 Low, 16 Medium (7+5+16=28), and three of those carry a Note that the severity can vary (InstanceCredentialExfiltration.InsideAWS and ResourceCredentialExfiltration.InsideAWS drop High to Medium for affiliated accounts; PasswordPolicyChange can be Low, Medium or High). Those asterisked severities are NOT 'Partial' coverage.
features.scope: A weak second dimension exists: each finding type names the data source that feeds it. 27 of the 28 sections carry a '+ **Data source: **' bullet; the 28th (CredentialAccess:IAMUser/CompromisedCredentials) instead carries '+ **Feature: **Included with Foundational Data Source Protection'. The distinct data-source values reduce to just two underlying sources - CloudTrail management events (named in all 27) and CloudTrail data events for S3 (named as an alternative in 6 of them: Policy:IAMUser/RootCredentialUsage, Policy:IAMUser/ShortTermRootCredentialUsage, both InstanceCredentialExfiltration types, and both ResourceCredentialExfiltration types). This is a per-finding attribute, not a coverage matrix, and it is stated in free text with inconsistent wording ('CloudTrail management event' singular vs 'CloudTrail management events' vs 'AWS CloudTrail management events'), so it does not support a clean second-dimension count. No Region, plan, tier, or scan-method dimension is present.
features.reasoning: The unit of claim on this page is one GuardDuty finding type - a name in the Namespace:ResourceTypeAffected/ThreatPurpose form that GuardDuty itself publishes. That is the catalogue axis 'findingType'. The page's rows do NOT collapse: each Topics bullet, each H2 and each H3 maps one-to-one onto a distinct finding-type string, and no two sections describe the same finding type. Nothing finer (per-API, per-severity, per-data-source) is enumerated as its own row, so expectedCount equals the row count equals the distinct-target count, and distinctTargets/collapse are correctly omitted.

shouldNotExtract: The 'Topics' anchor list is a duplicate of the H2 sections, not a second set of items - harvesting both yields 56 instead of 28. The '+ **Data source: **' bullets (27) and the single '+ **Feature: **' bullet are attributes, not axis values: a naive '^+ ' bullet scrape returns 56 bullets (28 topics + 27 data source + 1 feature). The 'Default severity' lines, the asterisks on 'High\*' / 'Low\*', and the severity-varying Notes are metadata, not statuses. The numbered '1.' investigation workflows inside the two InsideAWS sections are runbook steps. The example API names quoted in the AnomalousBehavior descriptions (GetPasswordData, GetSecretValue, BatchGetSecretValue, GenerateDbAuthToken, DeleteFlowLogs, DisableAlarmActions, StopLogging, AssociateIamInstanceProfile, AddUserToGroup, PutUserPolicy) are illustrative, explicitly 'such as' - they are not an apiOperation coverage list. The AWS service names dropped in prose (EC2, ECS, Lambda, Bedrock, S3, CloudTrail, STS, Outposts, Transit Gateway) are narrative, not a service coverage list. The 'See also' section - the optional Agent Toolkit for AWS skills-search boilerplate - is not coverage. Cross-links to compromised-creds.md, compromised-ec2.md, compromised-ecs.md, findings_suppression-rule.md, s3-protection.md and guardduty_data-sources.md are navigation.
coverageDimensions: REGION: nothing. The word 'Region' does not appear on this page at all; there is no Region table, no Region availability note, and no partition statement. Any per-Region figure attributed to this page is fabricated. SERVICE: nothing usable. AWS service names appear only inside prose descriptions as the context of a detection (EC2 instance credentials, ECS task credentials, Lambda, Bedrock logging, S3 data events, CloudTrail trails) - the page does not assert 'GuardDuty covers service X' and does not enumerate services as an axis. RESOURCE TYPE: exactly one value, stated once in the intro - every finding on this page 'always have a Resource Type of AccessKey'. That is a constant, not a distribution: the page gives a resource-type count of 1, and any larger resource-type figure from this page is invented. What the page DOES give is a finding-type catalogue of 28, plus a loose per-finding data-source attribution (CloudTrail management events, optionally CloudTrail data events for S3).
trap: The single most likely misparse is double counting: the 'Topics' list repeats all 28 finding types as anchor links before the body, so a parser that harvests both bullets and headings reports 56 (or 55, or 57 depending on whether it also grabs the 27 data-source bullets and the 1 feature bullet). Runners-up: (1) counting all 29 H2 headings and including the trailing 'See also' AI-coding-assistant boilerplate as a 29th finding type; (2) reading 'Default severity: High/Medium/Low' as a tri-state coverage status and reporting 7 Yes / 16 Partial / 5 No, when severity has nothing to do with support; (3) inventing a not-supported count - this page has zero explicit No statements, so any report of 'N not supported' is absence misread as a claim; (4) treating the two 'Note' blocks that vary severity plus the 'High\*' asterisks as 'Partial' coverage; (5) attributing a Region or per-service number to a page that says nothing about either; (6) missing that CredentialAccess:IAMUser/CompromisedCredentials has no 'Data source' bullet (it has a 'Feature' bullet instead), so a data-source-keyed parser silently drops one finding type and reports 27.
